title: Invariant rho section cuts out the opposite double-flag orbit
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with these adjectives and the split maximal torus $T$, Borel subgroup $B$, character $\rho$ and extension $\widetilde\rho$ as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Let $Q=S/B$ and $\pi:S\to Q$ be the right $B$-torsor of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Use the homogeneous invertible sheaf $L=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\rho}$ of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], where $(-\widetilde\rho)(b)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{-1}$. On the product scheme $X=Q\times_F Q$ [def-pc-scheme], put $D=\operatorname{pr}_1^*L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\operatorname{pr}_2^*L$, with its diagonal $S$-action. Invertible sheaves and their tensor powers have the meaning of [def-sc-invertible-module]. The scheme $X$ is integral (nonempty, irreducible and reduced), quasi-compact and separated over $F$; quasi-compact, separated, flat and surjective are as in [def-pc-morphism-conventions], and faithfully flat means flat and surjective. There are an element $n_0\in N_S(T)(F)$, for which $B\cap n_0Bn_0^{-1}=T$ as subgroup schemes, and an invariant global section $0\ne d\in\Gamma(X,D)$ such that the open subscheme $U=X_d$ where $d$ generates the rank-one stalk is the image of
$$q:S\longrightarrow X,\qquad g\longmapsto(gB,gn_0B).$$
This image is dense, $q:S\to U$ is a faithfully flat right $T$-torsor, and pullback is an equivariant $F$-algebra isomorphism
$$q^*:\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}F[S]^{T,\mathrm{right}},$$
where the right-hand side consists of $f$ with $f(gt)=f(g)$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Equivariance uses left translation $(s f)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$ and the induced action on functions on $U$. Invariance of $d$ is an identity of rational $S$-coactions, and the linearization on $D$ is the one induced from its two homogeneous factors. The assertions include the trivial group, when $Q=X=U=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $d$ is a nonzero constant.

source.place: Theorem 21.80, Example 21.83 and Theorem 21.84 (pp.450--451), Theorem 22.48 and Remark 22.49 (pp.479--480). Agent-formulated double-flag boundary consequence of the Bruhat and divisor descriptions; not quoted as a verbatim theorem of Milne.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] to $S$: it is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Fix the representative $n_0$ of $w_0$, so $B\cap n_0Bn_0^{-1}=T$. Write $V=R_u(B)$, $C=Vn_0B/B$, and $C_w=V^w n_wB$. The chart lemma makes $S,Q$ geometrically integral and gives a finite cover of $Q$ by affine-space charts with sections of $\pi$. Apply [lem-sc-geometrically-irreducible-product] to the two copies of $Q$; hence $X$ is irreducible and nonempty. Products of the finitely many affine-space charts cover $X$ and are affine spaces over $F$, whose polynomial coordinate rings are reduced. Thus $X$ is reduced and quasi-compact. Finally $Q$ is proper by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. The projection $X\to Q$ is its base change, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]; composing with $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Thus $X$ is separated. This proves the geometric assertions about $X$.

source.place: 21.70--21.84, flag charts; elementary chart and diagonal consequences

proof.text: The rational-weight assertion [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit] gives $w_0\rho=-\rho$. By [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules], $W_1=E_B(-\widetilde\rho)$ is nonzero. Apply [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line] with $\lambda=-\widetilde\rho$ and choose $0\ne f\in W_1^V$. The left-translation weight is $w_0(-\rho)=\rho$. Consequently, for every commutative $F$-algebra, $$f(bx)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{-1}f(x),\qquad f(xb)=\widetilde\rho(b)f(x).$$ Indeed the first identity follows from $(b^{-1}f)(x)=f(bx)$ and the decomposition $B=T\ltimes V$; the second is the defining identity of $W_1$. These are coaction identities, so include nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: 22.21--22.22, primitive functions and their torus weights

proof.text: For a representative $n_w$ and $t\in T$, calculate $f(tn_w)$ in two ways: $$\rho(t)^{-1}f(n_w)=f(tn_w)=(w\rho)(t)f(n_w).$$ Thus $f(n_w)\ne0$ implies $w\rho=-\rho$, hence $w=w_0$ by [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit]. Equality here is equality of characters, not of their differentials. On each Bruhat stratum the preceding semi-invariance gives $f(u n_w b)=\widetilde\rho(b)f(n_w)$. Moreover $f(n_0)\ne0$: otherwise $f$ vanishes on the dense longest cell and hence is zero on the integral scheme $S$. After rescaling, take $f(n_0)=1$. The same identities hold after every algebraically closed extension, so the nonvanishing open of $f$ in $S$ is exactly $C_{w_0}=Vn_0B$ as an open subscheme.

Define the regular function $\delta(g,h)=f(g^{-1}h)$ on $S\times_F S$. For $b_1,b_2\in B$, the identities in step 2 give $$\delta(gb_1,hb_2)=\widetilde\rho(b_1)\widetilde\rho(b_2)\delta(g,h).$$ Trivialize the two homogeneous line bundles over the flag charts of [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], their pullback coefficients have exactly this right semi-invariance for $\chi=-\widetilde\rho$. Hence the restrictions of $\delta$ glue to a section $d$ of $D$: the displayed formula is precisely the transition rule on overlaps in both factors. The identity $\delta(sg,sh)=\delta(g,h)$ proves invariance for the prescribed diagonal linearization after all scalar extensions. Also $\delta(1,n_0)=1$, so $d\ne0$.

Over a flag chart $A\subseteq Q$ choose its section $a:A\to S$ of $\pi$. The map $(x,y)\mapsto(x,a(x)^{-1}y)$ is an isomorphism $A\times Q\simeq A\times Q$. By step 3, in these coordinates $X_d$ is exactly $A\times C$. Every $z\in C$ is uniquely $u n_0B$ with $u\in V$, scheme-theoretically by [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. The map $\sigma(x,z)=a(x)u$ is therefore a morphism $A\times C\to S$ with $q\sigma(x,z)=(x,a(x)z)$. These local sections show that every point of $U=X_d$ is in the image of $q$, while $q(g)$ is in $U$ since $f(n_0)=1$. Thus $q(S)=U$. The open $U$ is nonempty, and is dense because $X$ is irreducible.

source.place: 21.80--21.84 and Example 21.83; explicit local lifts of pairs

proof.text: For every test scheme, $q(g)=q(h)$ means $t=g^{-1}h\in B$ and $n_0^{-1}tn_0\in B$. The subgroup-scheme intersection from [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] says exactly $t\in T$. Thus $(g,t)\mapsto(g,gt)$ identifies $S\times_FT$ with $S\times_US$, with inverse $(g,h)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}h)$. On each open of step 5, $g\mapsto(q(g),\sigma(q(g))^{-1}g)$ and $(x,t)\mapsto\sigma(x)t$ identify $q$ with projection onto the first factor from a product with $T$. This is a right $T$-torsor. Since $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$, its local coordinate map is $R\to R[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, a free faithful $R$-module extension (the Laurent monomials are a basis). Thus $q$ is flat and surjective, hence faithfully flat.

source.place: 21.84, opposite Borel intersection; explicit torsor coordinates

proof.text: Pullback along $q$ gives right-$T$-invariant functions. Conversely let $r\in F[S]$ satisfy $r(gt)=r(g)$ after every scalar extension. On an open $O$ of step 5 set $r_O=r\circ\sigma_O$. On an overlap, $\sigma_{O'}=\sigma_O t$ for the regular map $t=\sigma_O^{-1}\sigma_{O'}:O\cap O'\to T$ of step 6, so invariance gives $r_{O'}=r_O$. These functions glue to $\bar r\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, and the torsor coordinates give $q^*\bar r=r$. If $q^*a=0$, pullback by each $\sigma_O$ gives $a|_O=0$, so $a=0$. This constructs the inverse algebra map. Finally $q(sg)=s q(g)$ yields $q^*(s a)(g)=a(s^{-1}q(g))=(s q^*a)(g)$; hence the algebra isomorphism is equivariant for left translation. This proof uses ordinary sheaf gluing and explicit local sections, rather than an uncited descent theorem.

For the trivial group, $B=T=S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, $w_0=1$ and $\rho=0$. The construction takes $f=1$, $d=1$, $Q=X=U=\operatorname{Spec}F$, and $q$ and the algebra map are identities. Thus none of the arguments exclude rank zero.

proof_origin.place: Agent-written construction from 21.80--21.84 and 22.21--22.22; no divisor formula needed.
